We are resuming development of Break My Fix after a break.

Repository:
https://github.com/png270/breakfix

PROJECT OVERVIEW

Break My Fix is an autonomous AI security patch verification agent.

It accepts a GitHub security-fix PR, analyzes the patch,
generates security hypotheses, selects testing tools,
executes tests in an isolated environment, and produces
an evidence-backed security verdict.

The hackathon is over, but we want to finish this as a
production-quality portfolio project.

PREVIOUS PROGRESS

1. Built the BookShelf Flask demo application.

2. Created two security-fix PRs:
   PR #1: https://github.com/png270/breakfix/pull/1
   PR #2: https://github.com/png270/breakfix/pull/2

3. Implemented a FastAPI backend with:
   - GitHub PR ingestion
   - LLM adapter
   - Bounded agent loop
   - Security testing tools
   - Structured observations and verdicts

4. Built Docker fixtures pinned to both PR commits.

5. Implemented neatlogs instrumentation.

6. Backend tests passed: 58 tests in a temporary
   Python 3.13 environment.

UNRESOLVED ISSUES

1. Existing backend/.venv uses Python 3.14.
   The previously tested neatlogs SDK 1.4.26 required
   Python 3.10–3.13.

2. Synthetic neatlogs traces were generated locally
   but could not be retrieved from the neatlogs project.

3. Chromium failed to launch because of browser
   sandbox compatibility.

4. LiteLLM has not been verified with real tool calling.

5. Live PR analysis remains disabled.

YOUR TASK

PHASE 1 — RECOVER PROJECT STATE

Read:
- README.md
- hackathon.md
- backend/README.md
- .agents/skills/neathack/SKILL.md

Inspect:
- git status
- Current branch
- Uncommitted changes
- Backend module structure
- Python environment
- Existing tests
- Entire configuration

IMPORTANT:
Do not discard or overwrite uncommitted changes.

Do not modify the existing PR branches.

PHASE 2 — RECOVER NEATLOGS WORK

Inspect:
- backend/app/observability.py
- backend/app/agent.py
- backend/app/llm.py
- Existing neatlogs tests
- Current SDK dependencies

Determine what was implemented and what remains incomplete.

Check current official SDK compatibility before deciding
whether Python 3.13 is still required.

PHASE 3 — FIX ENVIRONMENT

If Python 3.13 is required:
- Preserve the existing environment until the replacement works.
- Recreate backend/.venv using Python 3.13.
- Install the project's dependencies.
- Verify neatlogs SDK compatibility.
- Run all backend tests.

PHASE 4 — DEBUG TRACE DELIVERY

Investigate why neatlogs synthetic traces are not
reaching the dashboard.

Check:
- SDK initialization
- API key configuration
- Exporter endpoint
- Project identification
- Flush/shutdown behavior
- Exporter errors
- Delivery counters
- Trace retrieval

Generate a fresh synthetic trace for verification.

Do not expose API keys or other credentials.

PHASE 5 — VERIFY

Run:
- Backend tests
- SDK Doctor
- Synthetic neatlogs trace test

Confirm whether the synthetic trace is visible in
the correct neatlogs project.

DO NOT:
- Run the full agent
- Analyze either security PR
- Make real LLM calls
- Weaken Docker restrictions
- Commit or push automatically

PHASE 6 — REPORT

Provide:
1. Current Git status and uncommitted changes.
2. What was recovered from the previous session.
3. Python environment status.
4. neatlogs integration status.
5. Test results.
6. Root cause of any trace delivery failure, if established.
7. Remaining blockers.
8. Recommended next development step.

Begin by inspecting the repository before making changes.

I’ll inspect the repository, configuration, and Python environments first, preserving uncommitted work and PR branches. I’ll also read the requested neathack skill before investigating trace delivery.
